introduction:
A Registered Will in Maharashtra provides undisputed legal backing to the distribution of your assets, ensuring your final wishes are executed accurately. Formally registering a Will minimizes future family disputes and prevents fraudulent claims.

The process involves pre-registering the document details online and visiting any of the Sub-Registrar Offices in Maharashtra to complete biometric authentication and physical signature verification.
quickFacts:
Quick Facts
  • Official Fee: A flat registration fee of ₹100. No stamp duty applies to Wills in Maharashtra.
  • Handling Fee: A scan/document handling charge of ₹40 per page.
  • Jurisdiction Freedom: You can legally register a Will at any of the 517 Sub-Registrar Offices (SRO) across Maharashtra (no regional restriction).
  • No Deadline: A Will can be registered at any time during your lifetime (no 4-month limit).
  • Mandatory Presence: The Testator (person making the Will) and two witnesses must physically visit the Sub-Registrar Office.
  • Sealed Will Option: Storing your Will in a sealed envelope inside the District Registrar vault is available for an extra fee of ₹100.
documentsRequired:
Documents Required

Note: Compile these original documents and photocopies before visiting the office or booking online.
Will & Medical Certificates
  • The Original Will: Prepared on clean, plain white paper or ledger paper (does not require stamp paper or notarization before registration).
  • Medical Fitness Certificate: Original certificate signed by a registered medical practitioner (MBBS/MD) confirming you are of sound mind. Crucial rule: Must be issued on or one day prior to the registration appointment.
Testator Documents
  • Identity & Address Proof: Original and photocopy of Aadhaar Card and PAN Card.
  • Photographs: Two recent color passport-size photographs of the Testator.
Witness Documents (Two Witnesses)
  • Identity & Address Proof: Original and photocopy of Aadhaar Card and PAN Card for both.
  • Photographs: Two recent color passport-size photographs of each witness.
  • Note: Witnesses should ideally be younger than the testator and cannot be beneficiaries (inheritors) in the Will.
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Online Pre-Registration & Token Booking

You must enter details and schedule a slot online before visiting the Sub-Registrar Office.

Step A: Public Data Entry (PDE)
  1. Go to the official IGR Maharashtra Public Data Entry Portal.
  2. Create a temporary login or select "Start New Document" under the local registration module.
  3. Select "Will" as your document type.
  4. Input the accurate legal names, ages, and address details of the Testator and the two witnesses exactly as shown on their Aadhaar Cards.
  5. Save the details to automatically generate a 13-digit PDE Token Number.
Step B: Online Fee Payment via GRAS
  1. Log into the Maharashtra GRAS (Government Receipt Accounting System) portal using your 13-digit PDE Token Number.
  2. Calculate the total fee: ₹100 registration fee + (₹40 × number of pages in the Will).
  3. Pay online via NetBanking, UPI, or Credit/Debit card.
  4. Print the final GRAS Challan receipt confirming payment.
Step C: Online Appointment Slot Booking (e-StepIn)
  1. Visit the e-StepIn Token Booking Application on the IGR website.
  2. Select your chosen Sub-Registrar Office district and branch location.
  3. Pick a convenient time slot, confirm the booking, and print your e-StepIn Appointment Receipt.
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Physical Registration at the SRO

Visit the chosen Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) on the scheduled slot to complete the registration:

  1. Arrive Early: Head to the Sub-Registrar Office 30 minutes prior to your scheduled time slot.
  2. Accompanying Parties: Ensure both witnesses are physically present with you.
  3. Document Submission: Present your file containing the original draft Will, medical fitness certificate, ID/Address proofs, passport photos, and your printed online GRAS challan/receipts.
  4. Verification Interview: The Sub-Registrar will verify your identity and briefly interview you to ensure the Will is executed voluntarily, without external pressure, and while in stable health.
  5. Biometrics Capture: Digital photographs and fingerprint impressions of the testator and both witnesses are captured at the desk.
  6. Final Endorsement: Sign the pages of your Will in front of the Sub-Registrar. The witnesses sign the official register. The SRO stamps the official seal and records the entry into Book No. 3 (Wills).
afterApplying:
After Registering — What Next?

Document Collection

The original physical copy is handed back to you immediately or made available for pickup within 7 to 15 days after scanning.

Future Changes (Codicils)

If you wish to make changes later, you can add an amendment called a Codicil, which follows this identical registration process to become legally valid.
